### Overview
Apple Intelligence is Apple's on-device AI platform, built on the capabilities of Apple Silicon (notably the 16-core Neural Engine across the A18 Pro, A19, M4, and M5 chip families). It runs most AI workloads locally on the user's device, falling back to Private Cloud Compute (Apple Silicon servers with end-to-end encryption) and a Google/Gemini deal for tasks too heavy for on-device processing. It is central to Apple's "razor-blade" AI strategy.

### Key Ideas & Contributions
- **On-device AI execution** — runs inference locally on the user's Neural Engine, so most AI workloads avoid cloud dependency.
- **Hybrid compute model** — layered by task complexity: local inference → Private Cloud Compute → rented Gemini models for heavy-lifting tasks such as next-generation Siri.
- **Razor-blade AI economics** — positioned as the recurring "blade" value layer delivered atop premium Apple Silicon hardware (the "razor").
- **$599 entry-point strategy** — MacBook Neo and iPhone 17e priced at $599 as ecosystem on-ramps that include full Apple Intelligence capabilities (per vault context).
- **Privacy-first positioning** — Private Cloud Compute processes with end-to-end encryption.

### Related Entities
- **Apple** — parent company and hardware platform
- **Apple Silicon** — foundation hardware; the platform is built on its Neural Engine capabilities
- **Neural Engine** — 16-core on-device AI accelerator
- **Private Cloud Compute** — Apple Silicon server-side AI processing with end-to-end encryption
- **Google / Gemini** — provides cloud AI models for advanced features
- **Siri** — primary user-facing interface for Apple Intelligence
